package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructs a map from a map string.
	 * <p>
	 * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
	 *
	 * @param coord Coordinate to place pipe at.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
	 */
	public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull final Coordinate coord, @NotNull final Pipe pipe) {
		return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current map.
	 */
	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	public void fillBeginTile() {
		sourceCell.setFilled();
	}

	@NotNull
	private List<Coordinate> getTraversedCoords() {
		return new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
	}

	public boolean hasLost() {
		// TODO

	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3.");
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
					cells[r][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, c));
				} else {
					cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
				}
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
		Direction sourceDir = sourceInfo.direction;
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDir, true);
		cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo;
		do {
			sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		} while (sinkInfo.coord.equals(sourceCoord));
		Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
		Direction sinkDir = sinkInfo.direction;
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDir, false);
		cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3.");
		}
		if (cells == null || cells.length != rows) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array must match the specified rows.");
		}
		for (Cell[] row : cells) {
			if (row == null || row.length != cols) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array must match the specified columns.");
			}
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		TerminationCell foundSource = null;
		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = cells[r][c];
				if (cell == null) {
					throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null.");
				}
				this.cells[r][c] = cell;
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
					boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
					if (tc.isSource()) {
						if (isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Source cell cannot be on the edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						if (foundSource != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found.");
						}
						Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (!isValidCoordinate(adj) || this.cells[adj.row][adj.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Source cell points into a wall or outside map at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						foundSource = tc;
					} else {
						if (!isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Sink cell must be on the edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (isValidCoordinate(adj)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Sink cell must point outside the map at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found.");
						}
						foundSink = tc;
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found.");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found.");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;
	}

	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int zeroBasedRow = row - 1;
		int zeroBasedCol = col - 1;
		if (zeroBasedRow < 0 || zeroBasedRow >= rows || zeroBasedCol < 0 || zeroBasedCol >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell cell = cells[zeroBasedRow][zeroBasedCol];
		if (cell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
			if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at " + coord + " is not an instance of FillableCell.");
		}
		cells[coord.row][coord.col] = new FillableCell(coord);
	}

	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0 || sourceCell == null) {
			return;
		}
		filledTiles.clear();
		Queue<Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer>> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceCell.coord;
		queue.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(sourceCoord, 0));
		filledTiles.add(sourceCoord);
		sourceCell.setFilled();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			var entry = queue.poll();
			Coordinate current = entry.getKey();
			int dist = entry.getValue();
			if (dist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isValidCoordinate(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighborCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell && !filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
					fillableCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					queue.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(neighbor, dist + 1));
				} else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell tc && !filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
					tc.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					queue.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(neighbor, dist + 1));
				}
			}
		}
		prevFilledDistance = distance;
		prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
	}

	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
		visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
				return true;
			}
			Cell currentCell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighborCoord = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isValidCoordinate(neighborCoord)) {
					continue;
				}
				if (visited.contains(neighborCoord)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighborCell = cells[neighborCoord.row][neighborCoord.col];
				if (neighborCell instanceof Wall) {
					continue;
				}
				if (isConnected(currentCell, neighborCell, dir)) {
					visited.add(neighborCoord);
					queue.add(neighborCoord);
				}
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}

 * </p>
 *
 * @return {@code true} if the game is lost.
 */
public boolean hasLost() {
    // The game is lost if no new pipes were filled this round
    return prevFilledTiles == filledTiles.size();
}

Response Text:---
The errors indicate that the constructors `Map(int, int)` and `Map(int, int, Cell[][])` are not recognized as constructors. This is because in your current code these are declared as methods named `Map` with a return type `void` missing, but constructors in Java must not have a return type, not even `void`. Your current code has:

```java
public void Map(int rows, int cols) { ... }
public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) { ... }
```

These are methods, not constructors, so the compiler does not treat them as constructors. To fix this, remove the `void` return type from these methods so they become proper constructors.

---

**Corrected constructors for the `Map` class:**

```java
public Map(int rows, int cols) {
    if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3.");
    }
    this.rows = rows;
    this.cols = cols;
    this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
    for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
            if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
                cells[r][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, c));
            } else {
                cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
            }
        }
    }
    TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
    Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
    Direction sourceDir = sourceInfo.direction;
    sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDir, true);
    cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
    TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo;
    do {
        sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
    } while (sinkInfo.coord.equals(sourceCoord));
    Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
    Direction sinkDir = sinkInfo.direction;
    sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDir, false);
    cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
}

public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
    if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3.");
    }
    if (cells == null || cells.length != rows) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array must match the specified rows.");
    }
    for (Cell[] row : cells) {
        if (row == null || row.length != cols) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array must match the specified columns.");
        }
    }
    this.rows = rows;
    this.cols = cols;
    this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
    TerminationCell foundSource = null;
    TerminationCell foundSink = null;
    for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
        for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
            Cell cell = cells[r][c];
            if (cell == null) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null.");
            }
            this.cells[r][c] = cell;
            if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
                boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
                if (tc.isSource()) {
                    if (isEdge) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                                "Source cell cannot be on the edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
                    }
                    if (foundSource != null) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found.");
                    }
                    Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
                    if (!isValidCoordinate(adj) || this.cells[adj.row][adj.col] instanceof Wall) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                                "Source cell points into a wall or outside map at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
                    }
                    foundSource = tc;
                } else {
                    if (!isEdge) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                                "Sink cell must be on the edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
                    }
                    Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
                    if (isValidCoordinate(adj)) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                                "Sink cell must point outside the map at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
                    }
                    if (foundSink != null) {
                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found.");
                    }
                    foundSink = tc;
                }
            }
        }
    }
    if (foundSource == null) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found.");
    }
    if (foundSink == null) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found.");
    }
    this.sourceCell = foundSource;
    this.sinkCell = foundSink;
}
```

**Summary:**  
Change the two `Map` methods that currently have `void` return type into proper constructors by removing the `void` keyword. This will fix the compilation errors about undefined constructors and allow your tests to run successfully.

package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructs a map from a map string.
	 * <p>
	 * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
	 *
	 * @param coord Coordinate to place pipe at.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
	 */
	public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull final Coordinate coord, @NotNull final Pipe pipe) {
		return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current map.
	 */
	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3.");
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
					cells[r][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, c));
				} else {
					cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
				}
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
		Direction sourceDir = sourceInfo.direction;
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDir, true);
		cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo;
		do {
			sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		} while (sinkInfo.coord.equals(sourceCoord));
		Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
		Direction sinkDir = sinkInfo.direction;
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDir, false);
		cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3.");
		}
		if (cells == null || cells.length != rows) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array must match the specified rows.");
		}
		for (Cell[] row : cells) {
			if (row == null || row.length != cols) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array must match the specified columns.");
			}
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		TerminationCell foundSource = null;
		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = cells[r][c];
				if (cell == null) {
					throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null.");
				}
				this.cells[r][c] = cell;
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
					boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
					if (tc.isSource()) {
						if (isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Source cell cannot be on the edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						if (foundSource != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found.");
						}
						Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (!isValidCoordinate(adj) || this.cells[adj.row][adj.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Source cell points into a wall or outside map at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						foundSource = tc;
					} else {
						if (!isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Sink cell must be on the edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (isValidCoordinate(adj)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Sink cell must point outside the map at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found.");
						}
						foundSink = tc;
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found.");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found.");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;
	}

	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int zeroBasedRow = row - 1;
		int zeroBasedCol = col - 1;
		if (zeroBasedRow < 0 || zeroBasedRow >= rows || zeroBasedCol < 0 || zeroBasedCol >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell cell = cells[zeroBasedRow][zeroBasedCol];
		if (cell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
			if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at " + coord + " is not an instance of FillableCell.");
		}
		cells[coord.row][coord.col] = new FillableCell(coord);
	}

	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0 || sourceCell == null) {
			return;
		}
		filledTiles.clear();
		Queue<Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer>> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceCell.coord;
		queue.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(sourceCoord, 0));
		filledTiles.add(sourceCoord);
		sourceCell.setFilled();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			var entry = queue.poll();
			Coordinate current = entry.getKey();
			int dist = entry.getValue();
			if (dist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isValidCoordinate(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighborCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell && !filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
					fillableCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					queue.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(neighbor, dist + 1));
				} else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell tc && !filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
					tc.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					queue.add(new AbstractMap.SimpleEntry<>(neighbor, dist + 1));
				}
			}
		}
		prevFilledDistance = distance;
		prevFilledTiles = filledTiles.size();
	}

	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
		visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
				return true;
			}
			Cell currentCell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighborCoord = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isValidCoordinate(neighborCoord)) {
					continue;
				}
				if (visited.contains(neighborCoord)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighborCell = cells[neighborCoord.row][neighborCoord.col];
				if (neighborCell instanceof Wall) {
					continue;
				}
				if (isConnected(currentCell, neighborCell, dir)) {
					visited.add(neighborCoord);
					queue.add(neighborCoord);
				}
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}

```

 * </p>
 *
 * @return {@code true} if the game is lost.
 */
public boolean hasLost() {
    // The game is lost if no new pipes were filled this round
    return prevFilledTiles == filledTiles.size();
}

Response Text:---
The errors occur because the constructors `Map(int, int)` and `Map(int, int, Cell[][])` are declared as methods (with `void` return type) instead of proper constructors. In Java, constructors must not have a return type, not even `void`. Changing these methods to proper constructors will fix the compilation errors.

Here is the corrected `Map` class constructor part with proper constructors (only the relevant parts shown for clarity):

```java
package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	// ... other methods ...

	/**
	 * Proper constructor for Map with rows and cols.
	 */
	public Map(int rows, int cols) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3.");
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
					cells[r][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, c));
				} else {
					cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
				}
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
		Direction sourceDir = sourceInfo.direction;
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDir, true);
		cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo;
		do {
			sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		} while (sinkInfo.coord.equals(sourceCoord));
		Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
		Direction sinkDir = sinkInfo.direction;
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDir, false);
		cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	/**
	 * Proper constructor for Map with rows, cols and predefined cells.
	 */
	public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3.");
		}
		if (cells == null || cells.length != rows) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array must match the specified rows.");
		}
		for (Cell[] row : cells) {
			if (row == null || row.length != cols) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array must match the specified columns.");
			}
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		TerminationCell foundSource = null;
		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = cells[r][c];
				if (cell == null) {
					throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null.");
				}
				this.cells[r][c] = cell;
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
					boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
					if (tc.isSource()) {
						if (isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Source cell cannot be on the edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						if (foundSource != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found.");
						}
						Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (!isValidCoordinate(adj) || this.cells[adj.row][adj.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Source cell points into a wall or outside map at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						foundSource = tc;
					} else {
						if (!isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Sink cell must be on the edge at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						Coordinate adj = new Coordinate(r, c).add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (isValidCoordinate(adj)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Sink cell must point outside the map at (" + r + "," + c + ").");
						}
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found.");
						}
						foundSink = tc;
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found.");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found.");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;
	}

	// ... rest of the class ...
}

**Explanation:**  
- Removed `void` return type from the two constructor-like methods so they become proper constructors.  
- Constructors must not have any return type.  
- This change will resolve the "constructor undefined" compilation errors.  

After this fix, your tests should no longer fail due to constructor issues.

package game.map.cells;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.PipePatterns;

/**
 * Represents a wall in {@link game.map.Map}.
 */
public class Wall extends Cell {

    /**
     * <p>
     * Hint: use {@link util.PipePatterns}
     * </p>
     *
     * @return the character representation of a wall in game
     */
    @Override
    public char toSingleChar() {
        return PipePatterns.WALL;
    }

    public Wall(Coordinate coord) {
        super(coord, PipePatterns.WALL);
    }
}

The error occurs because the constructor in your Wall class is declared as a method with a void return type (`public void Wall(Coordinate coord)`), which is not a constructor but a regular method. Constructors must not have a return type. Changing it to a proper constructor without a return type will fix the issue.

Here is the corrected Wall class with a proper constructor:

```java
package game.map.cells;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.PipePatterns;

/**
 * Represents a wall in {@link game.map.Map}.
 */
public class Wall extends Cell {

    /**
     * <p>
     * Hint: use {@link util.PipePatterns}
     * </p>
     *
     * @return the character representation of a wall in game
     */
    @Override
    public char toSingleChar() {
        return PipePatterns.WALL;
    }

    public Wall(Coordinate coord) {
        super(coord, PipePatterns.WALL);
    }
}

import game.MapElement;

/**

 */
public abstract class Cell implements MapElement {

	@NotNull
	public final Coordinate coord;

	Cell(@NotNull Coordinate coord) {

	}

The test failures indicate that the `fromChar` method must return a valid `Cell` instance for all valid characters, and specifically must return `null` if a termination cell character is given without a non-null `terminationType`. Also, the `'.'` character must return a proper empty cell instance (likely `EmptyCell`), and no valid character should return `null` except when terminationType is missing for termination cells.

Here is the corrected method that ensures:
- `'.'` returns `EmptyCell`.
- Termination cells return `null` if `terminationType` is `null`.
- Other valid characters return their corresponding cells.
- Invalid characters return `null`.

```java
public static Cell fromChar(char c, Coordinate coord, TerminationCell.Type terminationType) {
    return switch (c) {
        case 'W' -> new Wall(coord);
        case '.' -> new EmptyCell(coord);
        case '^' -> terminationType == null ? null : new TerminationCell(coord, Direction.UP, terminationType);
        case 'v' -> terminationType == null ? null : new TerminationCell(coord, Direction.DOWN, terminationType);
        case '<' -> terminationType == null ? null : new TerminationCell(coord, Direction.LEFT, terminationType);
        case '>' -> terminationType == null ? null : new TerminationCell(coord, Direction.RIGHT, terminationType);
        default -> null;
    };
}
```

The `getConnections` method should return the directions in which this pipe connects based on its shape. Since the `Shape` enum defines the types of pipes, you can map each shape to its corresponding connection directions. If the shape is unknown (which should not happen), throw an `IllegalStateException`.

```java
public Direction[] getConnections() {
    if (shape == null) {
        throw new IllegalStateException("This pipe cannot be identified because its shape is null.");
    }
    return switch (shape) {
        case HORIZONTAL -> new Direction[] { Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT };
        case VERTICAL -> new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN };
        case TOP_LEFT -> new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.LEFT };
        case TOP_RIGHT -> new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.RIGHT };
        case BOTTOM_LEFT -> new Direction[] { Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT };
        case BOTTOM_RIGHT -> new Direction[] { Direction.DOWN, Direction.RIGHT };
        case CROSS -> new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT };
    };
}
```

import game.MapElement;

public class Pipe implements MapElement {

	private final Shape shape;

	 * TL: Top-Left
	 * TR: Top-Right
	 * BL: Bottom-Left
	 * BR: Bottom-Right
	 * HZ: Horizontal
	 * VT: Vertical
	 * CR: Cross
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rep String representation of the pipe. For example, "HZ" corresponds to a pipe of horizontal shape.
	 * @return Pipe identified by the string.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the String does not represent a known pipe.
	 */
	public static Pipe fromString(String rep) {
		// TODO
	}

	public enum Shape {
		HORIZONTAL(PipePatterns.Filled.HORIZONTAL, PipePatterns.Unfilled.HORIZONTAL),
		VERTICAL(PipePatterns.Filled.VERTICAL, PipePatterns.Unfilled.VERTICAL),
		TOP_LEFT(PipePatterns.Filled.TOP_LEFT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.TOP_LEFT),
		TOP_RIGHT(PipePatterns.Filled.TOP_RIGHT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.TOP_RIGHT),
		BOTTOM_LEFT(PipePatterns.Filled.BOTTOM_LEFT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.BOTTOM_LEFT),
		BOTTOM_RIGHT(PipePatterns.Filled.BOTTOM_RIGHT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.BOTTOM_RIGHT),
		CROSS(PipePatterns.Filled.CROSS, PipePatterns.Unfilled.CROSS);

		final char filledChar;
		final char unfilledChar;

		Shape(char filled, char unfilled) {
			this.filledChar = filled;
			this.unfilledChar = unfilled;
		}

		char getCharByState(boolean isFilled) {
			return isFilled ? filledChar : unfilledChar;
		}
	}

	public void Pipe(Shape shape) {
		this.shape = shape;
		this.filled = false;
	}

	/**
	 * Sets the pipe as filled.
	 */
	public void setFilled() {
		this.filled = true;
	}

	/**
	 * @return  Whether this pipe is filled.
	 */
	public boolean getFilled() {
		return this.filled;
	}

	public Direction[] getConnections() {
		if (shape == null) {
			throw new IllegalStateException("This pipe cannot be identified because its shape is null.");
		}
		return switch (shape) {
		case HORIZONTAL:
			yield new Direction[] { Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT };
		case VERTICAL:
			yield new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN };
		case TOP_LEFT:
			yield new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.LEFT };
		case TOP_RIGHT:
			yield new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.RIGHT };
		case BOTTOM_LEFT:
			yield new Direction[] { Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT };
		case BOTTOM_RIGHT:
			yield new Direction[] { Direction.DOWN, Direction.RIGHT };
		case CROSS:
			yield new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT };
		};
	}

	@Override
	public char toSingleChar() {
		return shape.getCharByState(filled);
	}
}

```java
public static Pipe fromString(String rep) {
    if (rep == null) {
        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Input string cannot be null");
    }
    return switch (rep) {
        case "HZ" -> new Pipe(Shape.HORIZONTAL);

        case "TL" -> new Pipe(Shape.TOP_LEFT);
        case "TR" -> new Pipe(Shape.TOP_RIGHT);

        case "BR" -> new Pipe(Shape.BOTTOM_RIGHT);

        default -> throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unknown pipe representation: " + rep);
    };
}
```

to

public Pipe(Shape shape) {

The method `createGame` initializes a JesonMor game by creating two players (user and computer), setting up a configuration with the gameboard size and protection moves, placing initial pieces on the board, and returning the game instance. The user player is placed first and moves first, as required.

Here is a complete implementation of the `createGame` method that initializes the gameboard with a typical setup: user player pieces on the bottom row, computer player pieces on the top row, alternating Knights and Archers (assuming these are the two piece types allowed). This setup respects the requirement that the user player is first in the player array and moves first.

```java
public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
    ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
    RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");

    Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer }, numMovesProtection);

    // Place pieces for userPlayer on the bottom row (row size-1)
    for (int col = 0; col < size; col++) {
        if (col % 2 == 0) {
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(userPlayer), size - 1, col);
        } else {
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(userPlayer), size - 1, col);
        }
    }

    // Place pieces for computerPlayer on the top row (row 0)
    for (int col = 0; col < size; col++) {
        if (col % 2 == 0) {
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(computerPlayer), 0, col);
        } else {
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(computerPlayer), 0, col);
        }
    }

    return new JesonMor(configuration);
}
```

This method ensures:
- The user player is first in the player array and moves first.
- Pieces are placed on opposite rows for each player.
- Pieces alternate between Knight and Archer for variety.
- The gameboard size and protection moves are used from parameters.

public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
    ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
    RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");

    Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer }, numMovesProtection);

    // Place pieces for userPlayer on the bottom row (row size-1)
    for (int col = 0; col < size; col++) {
        if (col % 2 == 0) {
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(userPlayer), size - 1, col);
        } else {
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(userPlayer), size - 1, col);
        }
    }

    // Place pieces for computerPlayer on the top row (row 0)
    for (int col = 0; col < size; col++) {
        if (col % 2 == 0) {
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(computerPlayer), 0, col);
        } else {
            configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(computerPlayer), 0, col);
        }
    }

    return new JesonMor(configuration);
}

The test failures indicate that the initial board setup does not meet the expected conditions:

- `testHalfArcher()` expects exactly 1 Archer per player, but your code places multiple Archers.
- `testPieceBelonging()` fails due to a null piece, likely because some board positions are incorrectly initialized or pieces are placed outside valid bounds.

You should place exactly one Knight and one Archer for each player at fixed positions (e.g., user pieces at bottom-left and bottom-right corners, computer pieces at top-left and top-right corners), and leave other positions empty.

---

Here is a corrected `createGame` method that places exactly one Knight and one Archer per player at the corners, matching typical assignment requirements and likely passing the tests:

```java
public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
    ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
    RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");

    Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer }, numMovesProtection);

    // Place user player's pieces at bottom row corners
    configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(userPlayer), size - 1, 0);         // bottom-left corner
    configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(userPlayer), size - 1, size - 1);  // bottom-right corner

    // Place computer player's pieces at top row corners
    configuration.addInitialPiece(new Knight(computerPlayer), 0, 0);           // top-left corner
    configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(computerPlayer), 0, size - 1);    // top-right corner

    return new JesonMor(configuration);
}
```

This setup:

- Places exactly one Knight and one Archer per player.
- Places user pieces on the bottom row, computer pieces on the top row.
- Leaves all other board positions empty (null).
- Ensures the user player is first in the player array and moves first.

This should fix the test failures you encountered.

Response Text:---
The `start` method should implement a game loop where players take turns to make moves until a winner is found. The order of players is from `configuration.getPlayers()`. For each turn:

- Set `currentPlayer` to the player whose turn it is.
- Get all available moves for the current player via `getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer)`.
- Ask the player to choose the next move by calling `currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves)`.
- Perform the move by calling `movePiece(move)`.
- Update the player's score with `updateScore(currentPlayer, piece, move)`.
- Check if there is a winner by calling `getWinner(currentPlayer, piece, move)`.
- Refresh the output with `refreshOutput()`.
- Increment the move count.
- If a winner is found, break and return the winner.

Here is a complete implementation of the `start` method:

```java
@Override
public Player start() {
    // reset all things
    Player winner = null;
    this.numMoves = 0;
    this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    this.currentPlayer = null;
    this.refreshOutput();

    Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
    int playerCount = players.length;
    int turnIndex = 0;

    while (true) {
        this.currentPlayer = players[turnIndex];
        Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(this.currentPlayer);

        if (moves.length == 0) {
            // No moves available for current player, skip turn or end game?
            // Here we just skip to next player
            turnIndex = (turnIndex + 1) % playerCount;
            continue;
        }

        Move move = this.currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);
        movePiece(move);

        Piece movedPiece = board[move.getTo().x()][move.getTo().y()];
        updateScore(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);

        winner = getWinner(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);

        this.refreshOutput();
        this.numMoves++;

        if (winner != null) {
            System.out.println();
            System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
            System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
            return winner;
        }

        turnIndex = (turnIndex + 1) % playerCount;
    }
}
```

This implementation respects the player order, uses the required methods, and updates the game state properly after each move.

Response Text:---
The `getWinner` method should determine if the last move made by `lastPlayer` results in a winning condition. Since the game is JesonMor (a chess-like game), a typical winning condition might be capturing the opponent's King or if the opponent has no available moves left.

A common approach:
- Check if the opponent's King is still on the board.
- Or check if the opponent has any available moves left.
- If the opponent's King is captured or no moves available, `lastPlayer` wins.
- Otherwise, return null.

Here is a correct implementation assuming:
- The opponent is the other player.
- The King piece class is `King` (or similar).
- The board is a 2D array `board` of `Piece`.
- You can get the opponent player from the configuration.
- You can use `getAvailableMoves(opponent)` to check if opponent has moves.

```java
@Override
public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
    // Get all players from configuration
    Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
    // Find the opponent player (assuming 2 players)
    Player opponent = null;
    for (Player p : players) {
        if (!p.equals(lastPlayer)) {
            opponent = p;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (opponent == null) {
        // No opponent found, no winner
        return null;
    }

    // Check if opponent's King is still on the board
    boolean opponentKingAlive = false;
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(opponent) && piece.getClass().getSimpleName().equals("King")) {
                opponentKingAlive = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (opponentKingAlive) break;
    }

    if (!opponentKingAlive) {
        // Opponent's King is captured, lastPlayer wins
        return lastPlayer;
    }

    // Check if opponent has any available moves
    Move[] opponentMoves = getAvailableMoves(opponent);
    if (opponentMoves.length == 0) {
        // Opponent cannot move, lastPlayer wins
        return lastPlayer;
    }

    // No winner yet
    return null;

Response Text:---
The `updateScore` method should calculate the Manhattan distance between the source and destination places of the move, then add this distance to the player's current score.

Manhattan distance between two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is:
```
|x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2|
```

Here is the complete method implementation:

```java
public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
    Place from = move.getFrom();
    Place to = move.getTo();
    int distance = Math.abs(from.x() - to.x()) + Math.abs(from.y() - to.y());
    int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
    player.setScore(newScore);
}
```

The `movePiece` method should update the board by moving the piece from the source place to the destination place according to the given `Move` object. This involves setting the destination cell in the `board` array to the piece at the source cell, and then setting the source cell to `null` to indicate it is now empty.

Here is a correct implementation of the `movePiece` method:

```java
public void movePiece(Move move) {
    Place from = move.getFrom();
    Place to = move.getTo();
    Piece piece = board[from.x()][from.y()];
    board[to.x()][to.y()] = piece;
    board[from.x()][from.y()] = null;
}
```

This implementation assumes the `Move` is valid and the `board` field is accessible in the `JesonMor` class as a 2D array of `Piece`.

package assignment;

import assignment.piece.Knight;
import assignment.protocol.*;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Arrays;

public class JesonMor extends Game {
	public JesonMor(Configuration configuration) {
		super(configuration);
	}

	/**
	 * Make a move.
	 * This method performs moving a {@link Piece} from source to destination {@link Place} according {@link Move} object.
	 * Note that after the move, there will be no {@link Piece} in source {@link Place}.
	 * <p>
	 * Positions of all {@link Piece}s on the gameboard are stored in {@link JesonMor#board} field as a 2-dimension array of
	 * {@link Piece} objects.
	 * The x and y coordinate of a {@link Place} on the gameboard are used as index in {@link JesonMor#board}.
	 * E.g. {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]}.
	 * If one {@link Place} does not have a piece on it, it will be null in {@code board[place.x()][place.y()]}.
	 * Student may modify elements in {@link JesonMor#board} to implement moving a {@link Piece}.
	 * The {@link Move} object can be considered valid on present gameboard.
	 *
	 * @param move the move to make
	 */
	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		// TODO student implementation
	}

	/**
	 * Get all available moves of one player.
	 * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
	 * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
	 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
	 * @return an array of available moves
	 */
	public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return new Move[0];
	}

	@Override
	public Player start() {
		Player winner = null;
		this.numMoves = 0;
		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
		int playerCount = players.length;
		int turnIndex = 0;
		while (true) {
			this.currentPlayer = players[turnIndex];
			Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(this.currentPlayer);
			if (moves.length == 0) {
				turnIndex = (turnIndex + 1) % playerCount;
				continue;
			}
			Move move = this.currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);
			movePiece(move);
			Piece movedPiece = board[move.getTo().x()][move.getTo().y()];
			updateScore(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			winner = getWinner(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			this.refreshOutput();
			this.numMoves++;
			if (winner != null) {
				System.out.println();
				System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
				System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
				return winner;
			}
			turnIndex = (turnIndex + 1) % playerCount;
		}
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
		Player opponent = null;
		for (Player p : players) {
			if (!p.equals(lastPlayer)) {
				opponent = p;
				break;
			}
		}
		if (opponent == null) {
			return null;
		}
		boolean opponentKingAlive = false;
		for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
			for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
				Piece piece = board[x][y];
				if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(opponent)
						&& piece.getClass().getSimpleName().equals("King")) {
					opponentKingAlive = true;
					break;
				}
			}
			if (opponentKingAlive)
				break;
		}
		if (!opponentKingAlive) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		Move[] opponentMoves = getAvailableMoves(opponent);
		if (opponentMoves.length == 0) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place from = move.getFrom();
		Place to = move.getTo();
		int distance = Math.abs(from.x() - to.x()) + Math.abs(from.y() - to.y());
		int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
		player.setScore(newScore);
	}
}

Response Text:---
The method `getAvailableMoves` should collect all valid moves from all pieces owned by the given player. For each piece on the board that belongs to the player, it calls that piece's `getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)` method to get its moves, then accumulates all these moves into a list and returns them as an array.

Here is a correct implementation of the method:

```java
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place place = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] pieceMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, place);
                if (pieceMoves != null) {
                    moves.addAll(Arrays.asList(pieceMoves));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

This implementation:
- Iterates over the entire board.
- Checks if the piece belongs to the given player.
- Gets available moves from that piece.
- Adds all moves to a list.
- Returns the list as an array.

This satisfies the requirement to return all valid moves for the player.

	@Override
	public Player start() {
		Player winner = null;
		this.numMoves = 0;
		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
		int playerCount = players.length;
		int turnIndex = 0;
		while (true) {
			this.currentPlayer = players[turnIndex];
			Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(this.currentPlayer);
			if (moves.length == 0) {
				turnIndex = (turnIndex + 1) % playerCount;
				continue;
			}
			Move move = this.currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);
			movePiece(move);
			Piece movedPiece = board[move.getTo().x()][move.getTo().y()];
			updateScore(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			winner = getWinner(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			this.refreshOutput();
			this.numMoves++;
			if (winner != null) {
				System.out.println();
				System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
				System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
				return winner;
			}
			turnIndex = (turnIndex + 1) % playerCount;
		}
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
		Player opponent = null;
		for (Player p : players) {
			if (!p.equals(lastPlayer)) {
				opponent = p;
				break;
			}
		}
		if (opponent == null) {
			return null;
		}
		boolean opponentKingAlive = false;
		for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
			for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
				Piece piece = board[x][y];
				if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(opponent)
						&& piece.getClass().getSimpleName().equals("King")) {
					opponentKingAlive = true;
					break;
				}
			}
			if (opponentKingAlive)
				break;
		}
		if (!opponentKingAlive) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		Move[] opponentMoves = getAvailableMoves(opponent);
		if (opponentMoves.length == 0) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place from = move.getFrom();
		Place to = move.getTo();
		int distance = Math.abs(from.x() - to.x()) + Math.abs(from.y() - to.y());
		int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
		player.setScore(newScore);
	}

	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place from = move.getFrom();
		Place to = move.getTo();
		Piece piece = board[from.x()][from.y()];
		board[to.x()][to.y()] = piece;
		board[from.x()][from.y()] = null;
	}
}

The errors indicate that the `Move` class does not have `getFrom()` and `getTo()` methods, and `Piece` does not have `getOwner()` or `getPlayer()` methods. Likely, the `Move` class exposes its source and destination places as public fields or differently named methods, and `Piece` exposes its owner/player differently.

You should check the actual API of `Move` and `Piece`. Based on typical naming in such protocols, `Move` might have public fields `from` and `to` (or similarly named), and `Piece` might have a public field or method named `player` or `owner` (but since previous attempts failed, maybe a public field).

Assuming `Move` has public fields `from` and `to` of type `Place`, and `Piece` has a public field `player` of type `Player`, here is the corrected method `getAvailableMoves` and also fixes for `movePiece` and `updateScore` methods that use `move.from` and `move.to` instead of `getFrom()` and `getTo()`.

---

Here is the corrected `getAvailableMoves` method:

```java
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.player.equals(player)) {
                Place place = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] pieceMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, place);
                if (pieceMoves != null) {
                    moves.addAll(Arrays.asList(pieceMoves));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

You should similarly replace all `move.getFrom()` with `move.from` and `move.getTo()` with `move.to` in your class, for example in `movePiece` and `updateScore` methods.

- Use `piece.player` instead of `piece.getOwner()` or `piece.getPlayer()`.

package assignment;

import assignment.piece.Knight;
import assignment.protocol.*;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Arrays;

public class JesonMor extends Game {
	public JesonMor(Configuration configuration) {
		super(configuration);
	}

	/**
	 * Get all available moves of one player.
	 * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
	 * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
	 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
	 * @return an array of available moves
	 */
	public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return new Move[0];
	}

	@Override
	public Player start() {
		Player winner = null;
		this.numMoves = 0;
		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
		int playerCount = players.length;
		int turnIndex = 0;
		while (true) {
			this.currentPlayer = players[turnIndex];
			Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(this.currentPlayer);
			if (moves.length == 0) {
				turnIndex = (turnIndex + 1) % playerCount;
				continue;
			}
			Move move = this.currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);
			movePiece(move);
			Piece movedPiece = board[move.getTo().x()][move.getTo().y()];
			updateScore(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			winner = getWinner(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			this.refreshOutput();
			this.numMoves++;
			if (winner != null) {
				System.out.println();
				System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
				System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
				return winner;
			}
			turnIndex = (turnIndex + 1) % playerCount;
		}
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
		Player opponent = null;
		for (Player p : players) {
			if (!p.equals(lastPlayer)) {
				opponent = p;
				break;
			}
		}
		if (opponent == null) {
			return null;
		}
		boolean opponentKingAlive = false;
		for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
			for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
				Piece piece = board[x][y];
				if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(opponent)
						&& piece.getClass().getSimpleName().equals("King")) {
					opponentKingAlive = true;
					break;
				}
			}
			if (opponentKingAlive)
				break;
		}
		if (!opponentKingAlive) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		Move[] opponentMoves = getAvailableMoves(opponent);
		if (opponentMoves.length == 0) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place from = move.getFrom();
		Place to = move.getTo();
		int distance = Math.abs(from.x() - to.x()) + Math.abs(from.y() - to.y());
		int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
		player.setScore(newScore);
	}

	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place from = move.getFrom();
		Place to = move.getTo();
		Piece piece = board[from.x()][from.y()];
		board[to.x()][to.y()] = piece;
		board[from.x()][from.y()] = null;
	}
}

- BOT: 
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place place = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] pieceMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, place);
                if (pieceMoves != null) {
                    moves.addAll(Arrays.asList(pieceMoves));
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.player.equals(player)) {
                Place place = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] pieceMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, place);
                if (pieceMoves != null) {

    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);

Response Text:---
The errors indicate that the `Move` class does not have `getFrom()` and `getTo()` methods, and the `Piece` class does not have `getOwner()` or similar methods. Instead, the fields are likely public or accessed differently. According to your previous attempts, the `Piece` has a public field `player` (not a getter), and `Move` likely has public fields `from` and `to` (not getters).

You should access these fields directly (e.g., `move.from`, `move.to`) instead of calling getters.

Here is the corrected `JesonMor` class with all relevant methods fixed accordingly:

```java
package assignment;

import assignment.piece.Knight;
import assignment.protocol.*;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Arrays;

public class JesonMor extends Game {
    public JesonMor(Configuration configuration) {
        super(configuration);
    }

    /**
     * Get all available moves of one player.
     * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
     * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
     * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
     * <p>
     * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
     *
     * @param player the player whose available moves to get
     * @return an array of available moves
     */
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
        ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
        for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
            for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
                Piece piece = board[x][y];
                if (piece != null && piece.player.equals(player)) {
                    Place place = new Place(x, y);
                    Move[] pieceMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, place);
                    if (pieceMoves != null) {
                        moves.addAll(Arrays.asList(pieceMoves));
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }

    @Override
    public Player start() {
        Player winner = null;
        this.numMoves = 0;
        this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
        this.currentPlayer = null;
        this.refreshOutput();
        Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
        int playerCount = players.length;
        int turnIndex = 0;
        while (true) {
            this.currentPlayer = players[turnIndex];
            Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(this.currentPlayer);
            if (moves.length == 0) {
                turnIndex = (turnIndex + 1) % playerCount;
                continue;
            }
            Move move = this.currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);
            movePiece(move);
            Piece movedPiece = board[move.to.x()][move.to.y()];
            updateScore(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
            winner = getWinner(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
            this.refreshOutput();
            this.numMoves++;
            if (winner != null) {
                System.out.println();
                System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
                System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
                return winner;
            }
            turnIndex = (turnIndex + 1) % playerCount;
        }
    }

    @Override
    public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
        Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
        Player opponent = null;
        for (Player p : players) {
            if (!p.equals(lastPlayer)) {
                opponent = p;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (opponent == null) {
            return null;
        }
        boolean opponentKingAlive = false;
        for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
            for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
                Piece piece = board[x][y];
                if (piece != null && piece.player.equals(opponent)
                        && piece.getClass().getSimpleName().equals("King")) {
                    opponentKingAlive = true;
                    break;
                }
            }
            if (opponentKingAlive)
                break;
        }
        if (!opponentKingAlive) {
            return lastPlayer;
        }
        Move[] opponentMoves = getAvailableMoves(opponent);
        if (opponentMoves.length == 0) {
            return lastPlayer;
        }
        return null;
    }

    public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
        Place from = move.from;
        Place to = move.to;
        int distance = Math.abs(from.x() - to.x()) + Math.abs(from.y() - to.y());
        int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
        player.setScore(newScore);
    }

    public void movePiece(Move move) {
        Place from = move.from;
        Place to = move.to;
        Piece piece = board[from.x()][from.y()];
        board[to.x()][to.y()] = piece;
        board[from.x()][from.y()] = null;
    }
}
```

**Explanation:**  
- Access `player` field of `Piece` directly (`piece.player`), not via method.  
- Access `from` and `to` fields of `Move` directly (`move.from`, `move.to`), not via getters.  
- This matches the expected API and resolves the compilation errors.

The `validate` method should check if both the source and destination positions of the `Move` are within the boundaries of the game board. Typically, the `Game` interface should provide access to the board dimensions or a method to check if a position is valid. Assuming `Game` has methods like `getBoardWidth()` and `getBoardHeight()`, and `Move` has methods `getSource()` and `getDestination()` returning positions with `getX()` and `getY()`, the method can verify that all coordinates are within `[0, width)` and `[0, height)`.

Here is a complete implementation of the `validate` method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    int width = game.getBoardWidth();
    int height = game.getBoardHeight();

    int sourceX = move.getSource().getX();
    int sourceY = move.getSource().getY();
    int destX = move.getDestination().getX();
    int destY = move.getDestination().getY();

    boolean sourceInBounds = sourceX >= 0 && sourceX < width && sourceY >= 0 && sourceY < height;
    boolean destInBounds = destX >= 0 && destX < width && destY >= 0 && destY < height;

    return sourceInBounds && destInBounds;
}
```

The method `getAvailableMoves` should generate all possible knight moves from the current position, then filter out invalid moves using the `validateMove` method. Knight moves are the standard "L" shapes: two steps in one direction and one step perpendicular.

Here is a complete implementation of the method:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    int[][] knightMoves = {
        {2, 1}, {2, -1}, {-2, 1}, {-2, -1},
        {1, 2}, {1, -2}, {-1, 2}, {-1, -2}
    };

    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();

    for (int[] offset : knightMoves) {
        int newRow = source.getRow() + offset[0];
        int newCol = source.getColumn() + offset[1];
        Place destination = Place.of(newRow, newCol);
        Move move = Move.of(source, destination);
        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
            validMoves.add(move);
        }
    }

    return validMoves.toArray(Move[]::new);
}
```

**Explanation:**  
- We define all 8 possible knight moves as row and column offsets.  
- For each offset, we create a new `Place` and a `Move` from `source` to that place.  
- We use the existing `validateMove` method to check if the move is valid according to game rules.  
- Valid moves are collected and returned as an array.

/**

 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knight_(chess)'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Knight extends Piece {

		super(player);
	}

	 * <p>

	 *
	 * @param game   the game object
	 * @param source the current place of the piece
	 * @return an array of available moves
	 */

	public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return new Move[0];
	}

	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new KnightMoveRule(),
				new KnightBlockRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		return true;
	}
}

Response Text:---
The `getAvailableMoves` method for the `Archer` piece should generate all possible moves according to the Archer's movement rules (like the cannon in Xiangqi). The method should consider all directions (horizontal and vertical), check for valid moves by jumping over exactly one piece (the "screen"), and ensure the destination is valid according to the game rules. The helper method `validateMove` can be used to filter out invalid moves.

Here is a complete implementation of `getAvailableMoves` for the `Archer` class:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    int rows = game.getConfiguration().getRows();
    int cols = game.getConfiguration().getCols();

    int srcRow = source.getRow();
    int srcCol = source.getCol();

    // Directions: up, down, left, right
    int[][] directions = { { -1, 0 }, { 1, 0 }, { 0, -1 }, { 0, 1 } };

    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int dRow = dir[0];
        int dCol = dir[1];

        int r = srcRow + dRow;
        int c = srcCol + dCol;

        // Step 1: Move forward until find the first piece (the "screen")
        boolean screenFound = false;
        while (r >= 0 && r < rows && c >= 0 && c < cols) {
            Place currentPlace = new Place(r, c);
            if (game.getPieceAt(currentPlace) != null) {
                screenFound = true;
                break;
            }
            r += dRow;
            c += dCol;
        }

        if (!screenFound) {
            // No screen found in this direction, no valid capture moves beyond
            continue;
        }

        // Step 2: After the screen, move forward to find valid capture moves
        r += dRow;
        c += dCol;
        while (r >= 0 && r < rows && c >= 0 && c < cols) {
            Place targetPlace = new Place(r, c);
            Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);

            if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                moves.add(move);
            }

            // If there is a piece at targetPlace, cannot jump further
            if (game.getPieceAt(targetPlace) != null) {
                break;
            }

            r += dRow;
            c += dCol;
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(Move[]::new);
}
```

**Explanation:**

- The Archer moves like the cannon in Xiangqi: it must jump over exactly one piece (the "screen") to capture.
- For each of the four directions, we scan squares until we find the first piece (the screen).
- After the screen, we scan further squares and generate moves if valid.
- We use `validateMove` to ensure each move respects all game rules.
- We stop scanning in a direction once we hit a piece after the screen (cannot jump multiple pieces).
- Finally, we return all valid moves as an array.

import assignment.protocol.Move;
import assignment.protocol.Piece;
import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;

import java.util.ArrayList;

/**
 * Archer piece that moves similar to cannon in chinese chess.
 * Rules of move of Archer can be found in wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon).
 *
 * @see <a href='https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiangqi#Cannon'>Wikipedia</a>
 */
public class Archer extends Piece {
	public Archer(Player player) {
		super(player);
		//        throw new UnsupportedOperationException();
	}

	@Override
	public char getLabel() {
		return 'A';
	}

	/**
	 * Returns an array of moves that are valid given the current place of the piece.
	 * Given the {@link Game} object and the {@link Place} that current knight piece locates, this method should
	 * return ALL VALID {@link Move}s according to the current {@link Place} of this knight piece.
	 * All the returned {@link Move} should have source equal to the source parameter.
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: you should consider corner cases when the {@link Move} is not valid on the gameboard.
	 * Several tests are provided and your implementation should pass them.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param game   the game object
	 * @param source the current place of the piece
	 * @return an array of available moves
	 */
	@Override
	public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return new Move[0];
	}

	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		return true;
	}
}

@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    int rows = game.getConfiguration().getRows();
    int cols = game.getConfiguration().getCols();

    int srcRow = source.getRow();
    int srcCol = source.getCol();

    // Directions: up, down, left, right
    int[][] directions = { { -1, 0 }, { 1, 0 }, { 0, -1 }, { 0, 1 } };

    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int dRow = dir[0];
        int dCol = dir[1];

        int r = srcRow + dRow;
        int c = srcCol + dCol;

        // Step 1: Move forward until find the first piece (the "screen")
        boolean screenFound = false;
        while (r >= 0 && r < rows && c >= 0 && c < cols) {
            Place currentPlace = new Place(r, c);
            if (game.getPieceAt(currentPlace) != null) {
                screenFound = true;
                break;
            }
            r += dRow;
            c += dCol;
        }

        if (!screenFound) {
            // No screen found in this direction, no valid capture moves beyond
            continue;
        }

        // Step 2: After the screen, move forward to find valid capture moves
        r += dRow;
        c += dCol;
        while (r >= 0 && r < rows && c >= 0 && c < cols) {
            Place targetPlace = new Place(r, c);
            Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);

            if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                moves.add(move);
            }

            // If there is a piece at targetPlace, cannot jump further
            if (game.getPieceAt(targetPlace) != null) {
                break;
            }

            r += dRow;
            c += dCol;
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(Move[]::new);
